I ENLARGE MY CIRCLE OF ACQUAINTANCE", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u008-b0030", "target": "Однако меня не считали формально принятым в школу, пока не приехал Дж. Стирфорт. К этому мальчику, который слыл большим учёным, был очень хорош собой и по меньшей мере на полдюжины лет старше меня, меня привели, как к судье. Под навесом на площадке для игр он расспросил о подробностях моего наказания и соизволил высказать мнение, что это «чертовски стыдно»; за что я навсегда остался ему обязан.", "source_sha256": "3cb7caaa89ff7779fc9a171f71520c51bc9284981ab73d028408f447fb46147d", "target_id": "ru-en85-u008-b0030", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "1cfe3a90dd8e833da236bd4a557943659997114c8935192307ae1e4fd6afbdb6"}, {"source_id": "en85-u008-b0031", "target": "— Сколько у тебя денег, Копперфилд? — спросил он, отводя меня в сторону, когда покончил с моим делом в таких выражениях. Я ответил, что семь шиллингов.", "source_sha256": "db6ec7fb00bb9436e588d90809311a77e929e2a24c09f6f5d7098023adaa3f76", "target_id": "ru-en85-u008-b0031", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "92be29c992e78d58008e7725311ecebd438bda447656ca767021d602ffddbfef"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 6, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u008-b0032", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You had better give it to me to take care of,’ he said. ‘At least, you can if you like. You needn’t if you don’t like.’", "sha256": "0420636453c3baaa010c94a3b19654a41d81eb1c154e884dd8e0f929bb681e7e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[32]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0033", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I hastened to comply with his friendly suggestion, and opening Peggotty’s purse, turned it upside down into his hand.", "sha256": "067f2fc2a9ac20f4e3f2b77816670d16d4215f773875171d76849d6a5a50da18", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[33]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0034", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Do you want to spend anything now?’ he asked me.", "sha256": "1118a4514f43936acb437a8ea33d88fa91a61296073e20936785bfa50df0eb28", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[34]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0035", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No thank you,’ I replied.", "sha256": "53d99a4786a5e44f38f5e6e16e095033e0771c51bc85f3620ee507f5578e28d5", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[35]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0036", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You can, if you like, you know,’ said Steerforth. ‘Say the word.’", "sha256": "43b11d8323034b676286a4e93121518651b9c8d8e25b6067699115051b842974", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[36]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0037", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No, thank you, sir,’ I repeated.", "sha256": "c9a0551bbbd5204843f68ec434733069b02afb20a1ff90e5d2d282432f5044ea", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[37]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0038", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Perhaps you’d like to spend a couple of shillings or so, in a bottle of currant wine by and by, up in the bedroom?’ said Steerforth. ‘You belong to my bedroom, I find.’", "sha256": "92cc10031504352b665986159eb912064dcf5a2bb605644c64d1001e15fb7a63", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[38]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0039", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "It certainly had not occurred to me before, but I said, Yes, I should like that.", "sha256": "b391f2e3016b1c2e3e60de93b757ca987db9f985fbc46f73f8e025cbc25819d7", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[39]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0040", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Very good,’ said Steerforth. ‘You’ll be glad to spend another shilling or so, in almond cakes, I dare say?’", "sha256": "dd82dc782a9e44574c0c3fef5ed9ec2a08c561c5a847db8de59202dbc29ccaa6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[40]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0041", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I said, Yes, I should like that, too.", "sha256": "7535ee6d38307231877171f812a4f3a20e7a6acf429a63f92d8907220bf08cc3", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[41]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0042", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘And another shilling or so in biscuits, and another in fruit, eh?’ said Steerforth. ‘I say, young Copperfield, you’re going it!’", "sha256": "fa30c42870454bf74d663e21b1198596af40b9e20cdc35f4e434e1d546716197", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[42]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0043", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I smiled because he smiled, but I was a little troubled in my mind, too.", "sha256": "2cbb693e508a91a0308ed9c9b6c94fcea35d533333d8f2137e81691e7ef7bb7c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[43]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0044", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Well!’ said Steerforth. ‘We must make it stretch as far as we can; that’s all. I’ll do the best in my power for you. I can go out when I like, and I’ll smuggle the prog in.’ With these words he put the money in his pocket, and kindly told me not to make myself uneasy; he would take care it should be all right. He was as good as his word, if that were all right which I had a secret misgiving was nearly all wrong—for I feared it was a waste of my mother’s two half-crowns—though I had preserved the piece of paper they were wrapped in: which was a precious saving. When we went upstairs to bed, he produced the whole seven shillings’ worth, and laid it out on my bed in the moonlight, saying:", "sha256": "436d251ba2bc03ca12649cba8f10eee1ee95437889c8dcba47eab353f42fe5c1", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[44]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0045", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘There you are, young Copperfield, and a royal spread you’ve got.’", "sha256": "2f840f52b35cd7988275bfbac9899eb9c832a618b22bd9c96194beaf373799eb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[45]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0046", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I couldn’t think of doing the honours of the feast, at my time of life, while he was by; my hand shook at the very thought of it. I begged him to do me the favour of presiding; and my request being seconded by the other boys who were in that room, he acceded to it, and sat upon my pillow, handing round the viands—with perfect fairness, I must say—and dispensing the currant wine in a little glass without a foot, which was his own property. As to me, I sat on his left hand, and the rest were grouped about us, on the nearest beds and on the floor.", "sha256": "bc0be040427bc20a740f47aebbfa3b13a7ffd3d1e9a2dbebe3db887524279500", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[46]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0047", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "How well I recollect our sitting there, talking in whispers; or their talking, and my respectfully listening, I ought rather to say; the moonlight falling a little way into the room, through the window, painting a pale window on the floor, and the greater part of us in shadow, except when Steerforth dipped a match into a phosphorus-box, when he wanted to look for anything on the board, and shed a blue glare over us that was gone directly! A certain mysterious feeling, consequent on the darkness, the secrecy of the revel, and the whisper in which everything was said, steals over me again, and I listen to all they tell me with a vague feeling of solemnity and awe, which makes me glad that they are all so near, and frightens me (though I feign to laugh) when Traddles pretends to see a ghost in the corner.", "sha256": "f889d6511c597ee82181772cbd38e2b86237c4d577c47bf37209183b85d6a0dc", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[47]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0048", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I heard all kinds of things about the school and all belonging to it. I heard that Mr. Creakle had not preferred his claim to being a Tartar without reason; that he was the sternest and most severe of masters; that he laid about him, right and left, every day of his life, charging in among the boys like a trooper, and slashing away, unmercifully. That he knew nothing himself, but the art of slashing, being more ignorant (J. Steerforth said) than the lowest boy in the school; that he had been, a good many years ago, a small hop-dealer in the Borough, and had taken to the schooling business after being bankrupt in hops, and making away with Mrs. Creakle’s money. With a good deal more of that sort, which I wondered how they knew.", "sha256": "264842b76daeca09575088fb817ce06db1a528c706d168a03752b01b18633cb1", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[48]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0049", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I heard that the man with the wooden leg, whose name was Tungay, was an obstinate barbarian who had formerly assisted in the hop business, but had come into the scholastic line with Mr. Creakle, in consequence, as was supposed among the boys, of his having broken his leg in Mr. Creakle’s service, and having done a deal of dishonest work for him, and knowing his secrets. I heard that with the single exception of Mr. Creakle, Tungay considered the whole establishment, masters and boys, as his natural enemies, and that the only delight of his life was to be sour and malicious. I heard that Mr. Creakle had a son, who had not been Tungay’s friend, and who, assisting in the school, had once held some remonstrance with his father on an occasion when its discipline was very cruelly exercised, and was supposed, besides, to have protested against his father’s usage of his mother. I heard that Mr. Creakle had turned him out of doors, in consequence; and that Mrs. and Miss Creakle had been in a sad way, ever since.", "sha256": "8a186ec0c2b34315fef3625213c6f7f822b17e07c31db0b4e7f2f7f73e0c6b1c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[49]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0050", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "But the greatest wonder that I heard of Mr. Creakle was, there being one boy in the school on whom he never ventured to lay a hand, and that boy being J. Steerforth. Steerforth himself confirmed this when it was stated, and said that he should like to begin to see him do it. On being asked by a mild boy (not me) how he would proceed if he did begin to see him do it, he dipped a match into his phosphorus-box on purpose to shed a glare over his reply, and said he would commence by knocking him down with a blow on the forehead from the seven-and-sixpenny ink-bottle that was always on the mantelpiece. We sat in the dark for some time, breathless.", "sha256": "fff9a089b93c18e3b483e530486e7963b57a0383fbc4dd072399f8de642e1e21", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[50]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0051", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I heard that Mr. Sharp and Mr. Mell were both supposed to be wretchedly paid; and that when there was hot and cold meat for dinner at Mr. Creakle’s table, Mr. Sharp was always expected to say he preferred cold; which was again corroborated by J. Steerforth, the only parlour-boarder. I heard that Mr. Sharp’s wig didn’t fit him; and that he needn’t be so ‘bounceable’—somebody else said ‘bumptious’—about it, because his own red hair was very plainly to be seen behind.", "sha256": "d3123aa87f95ca13093b84d53a59f55897255e5fe7b7390d3e8152cd0ac8a633", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[51]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0052", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I heard that one boy, who was a coal-merchant’s son, came as a set-off against the coal-bill, and was called, on that account, ‘Exchange or Barter’—a name selected from the arithmetic book as expressing this arrangement. I heard that the table beer was a robbery of parents, and the pudding an imposition. I heard that Miss Creakle was regarded by the school in general as being in love with Steerforth; and I am sure, as I sat in the dark, thinking of his nice voice, and his fine face, and his easy manner, and his curling hair, I thought it very likely. I heard that Mr. Mell was not a bad sort of fellow, but hadn’t a sixpence to bless himself with; and that there was no doubt that old Mrs. Mell, his mother, was as poor as job. I thought of my breakfast then, and what had sounded like ‘My Charley!’ but I was, I am glad to remember, as mute as a mouse about it.", "sha256": "18742b9e411bb471cd76da2f2dcf01011f28ade2fb2ac941b8e1e16908e378d3", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[52]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0053", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The hearing of all this, and a good deal more, outlasted the banquet some time. The greater part of the guests had gone to bed as soon as the eating and drinking were over; and we, who had remained whispering and listening half-undressed, at last betook ourselves to bed, too.", "sha256": "ded257c422ea93f5e6c823f914e615394b28bf7fc80045464be22ee4d8f46dc1", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[53]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0054", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Good night, young Copperfield,’ said Steerforth. ‘I’ll take care of you.’ ‘You’re very kind,’ I gratefully returned. ‘I am very much obliged to you.’", "sha256": "f964f3647eaf8f79ba3be4cd293ceb3ec1cf4a57ae9788c5009dc2658bb7a01e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[54]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0055", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You haven’t got a sister, have you?’ said Steerforth, yawning.", "sha256": "9945da2a225fcde42ac52c87bfc16c5f79b6c8c90998547da660a6eb9de04171", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[55]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0056", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No,’ I answered.", "sha256": "c5e2c9261817b23f9057aa2a8dd2016697dc40f5ee375329b3f8a5de069c8aa9", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[56]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0057", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘That’s a pity,’ said Steerforth. ‘If you had had one, I should think she would have been a pretty, timid, little, bright-eyed sort of girl. I should have liked to know her. Good night, young Copperfield.’", "sha256": "121bd4b08cd870dd1f19fdee24c1453f88b9aef33d30c69ae4013f9f53982bbf", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[57]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0058", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Good night, sir,’ I replied.", "sha256": "8b269c8a2eab0cfa4cc1a5f3639d9d87970072e26b7c857205c43112e55cd0b8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[58]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u008-b0059", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I thought of him very much after I went to bed, and raised myself, I recollect, to look at him where he lay in the moonlight, with his handsome face turned up, and his head reclining easily on his arm. He was a person of great power in my eyes; that was, of course, the reason of my mind running on him. No veiled future dimly glanced upon him in the moonbeams. There was no shadowy picture of his footsteps, in the garden that I dreamed of walking in all night.", "sha256": "e80d8441e9d73946e3b5c33975d8d9d92af2a8ed6241f5cb30c71c2d209a883b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[13]/p[59]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
